summary: Describes an RTP payload format for Reduced-Complexity Decoding Operation of H.264 Baseline profile, which reduces decoding cost. It builds on the H.264 payload format. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: A way to send video that is easier for a weak device to unpack.

questions: how to send h.264 rcdo over rtp
subtitle: How to send H.264 Baseline video that is cheaper to decode over RTP, as a separate H264-RCDO media type.

tldr.problem: ITU-T H.241 defines a Reduced-Complexity Decoding Operation (RCDO) for H.264 Baseline video that lowers decoding cost, but there was no way to signal and carry it in RTP sessions.
tldr.mechanism: It reuses the H.264 RTP payload format of RFC 6184 unchanged and registers a new media subtype, H264-RCDO, whose parameters are copied from H264 except for new rules on profile-level-id.
tldr.outcome: RCDO streams can be negotiated with SDP and sent alongside ordinary H.264, with H264 offered as a fallback.

today: RFC 6185 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It depends on RFC 6184 for the actual payload format.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
ITU-T Recommendation H.241 specifies a Reduced-Complexity Decoding Operation (RCDO) for H.264 Baseline profile bitstreams. It also specifies a bitstream constraint and a way to signal RCDO inside the bitstream. The signal tells the decoder that the stream meets the constraint and that it shall apply the RCDO decoding process.

RCDO is meant to support higher resolutions at the same high frame rates by reducing the processing needed, and so the decoding cost and resource use. RFC 6185 defines media type parameters so that RCDO can be used in systems that signal with the Session Description Protocol (SDP).
sections.eli5: Some video can be packed so a slow device has less work to open it. This document says how to label and send that kind of video over the network.

sections.title: Media Format Background
sections.content:
RCDO is specified in Annex B of H.241. It is a separate H.264 mode and is distinct from any H.264 profile, though an RCDO bitstream obeys all the constraints of the Baseline profile. H.241 signals additional modes with an AdditionalModesSupported parameter, and RCDO is currently the only one defined.

The media format builds on the H.264 RTP payload format in RFC 6184, which is the basis for this document. A separate media subtype, H264-RCDO, is defined so that deployed H.264 implementations stay backward compatible.
sections.eli5: The new kind of video gets its own name tag, so older players that only know the plain name are not confused by it.

sections.title: Payload Format and Congestion Control
sections.content:
The payload format in Section 5 of RFC 6184 SHALL be used, including its RTP header usage. This document adds no new packet layout.

Congestion control for RTP SHALL follow RFC 3550 and any applicable RTP profile such as RFC 3551. With best-effort service, users SHALL monitor packet loss to keep the loss rate within acceptable parameters.
sections.eli5: The video is put into network packets exactly the way ordinary H.264 video is. Senders also have to watch for lost packets and slow down if the network is struggling.

sections.title: The H264-RCDO Media Type and Parameters
sections.content:
The subtype H264-RCDO is registered with type name video in the IETF tree. The required parameter rate is the RTP timestamp clock rate and MUST be 90000.

Except for profile-level-id, the optional parameters are copied verbatim from RFC 6184 so that the registration is self-contained. They cover receiver limits (max-recv-level, max-mbps, max-fs, max-cpb, max-dpb, max-br), parameter sets (sprop-parameter-sets and related), packetization mode, interleaving and buffering, and aspect-ratio support (sar-understood, sar-supported).

The new rule is in profile-level-id. RCDO is distinct from any profile, so the profile_idc byte is 0. An RCDO bitstream MUST obey all Baseline constraints, so only constraint_set0_flag is 1 in the profile-iop byte. For example, level 1.3 gives 00800d and level 2.1 gives 008015. If no profile-level-id is present, level 1 (00800a) MUST be implied.

For packetization-mode, a value of 0 or no value means single NAL mode, 1 means non-interleaved mode, and 2 means interleaved mode.
sections.eli5: The label carries a list of settings, such as how big a picture the receiver can handle. Most settings are copied from plain H.264, but the 'which kind of video' setting has a special value for this one.

sections.title: Mapping to SDP and Offer/Answer
sections.content:
Mapping to SDP follows Section 3 of RFC 4855. An example fmtp line for a level 2.2 bitstream is a=fmtp:97 profile-level-id=008016.

In the offer/answer model, the rules of Section 8.2.2 of RFC 6184 apply. For interoperability with systems that do not support H264-RCDO, offering the H264 subtype as well is RECOMMENDED. Listing the H264-RCDO payload number before H264 on the m= line signals that H264-RCDO is preferred, as in RFC 3264.

For declarative use, such as RTSP or SAP, Section 8.2.3 of RFC 6184 applies.
sections.eli5: When two devices agree on a video format, the sender lists its favourite first and the plain version second. If the other side does not know the favourite, it picks the plain one.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Packets using this payload format are subject to the security considerations of the RTP specification and any applicable RTP profile. The security considerations of RFC 6184 also apply. The RFC states that it introduces no additional security considerations.
sections.eli5: Nothing new to worry about beyond what already applies to sending video over RTP.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: IANA has registered H264-RCDO as specified in the media type definition and added it to the IANA registry for RTP Payload Format MIME types. The registration says the type is only defined for transfer via RTP, is framed and binary, and is intended for common use in video streaming and conferencing applications. Use within other framing protocols is not defined.
sections.eli5: The new name was entered in the official list of video format names, with a note that it only works inside RTP.

data.title: Offering RCDO with H.264 fallback
data.code:
m=video 5555 RTP/AVP 97 98
a=rtpmap:97 H264-RCDO/90000
a=fmtp:97 profile-level-id=008016;max-mbps=42000;max-smbps=323500
a=rtpmap:98 H264/90000
a=fmtp:98 profile-level-id=428016;max-mbps=35000;max-smbps=323500
